# Table of School System Structure 

Primary school begins at age 3 with Nursery School and continues on into elementary school.Students progress to Lower Secondary School at age 11 to Upper Secondary School at age 15 where they have the option of choosing between three baccalaureate programmes: general, technological, and vocational.

 décembre 2025 

 

 

### Primary School (age 3–11)

#### Nursery school (compulsory at the start of the 2019 school year)

- Age 3 to 4 First year → 1st Cycle: Early learning
- Age 4 to 5 Second year → 1st Cycle: Early learning
- Age 5 to 6 Third year → 1st Cycle: Early learning

#### Elementary school (compulsory)

- Age 6 to 7 First grade (Cours préparatoire) → 2nd Cycle: Basic learning
- Age 7 to 8 Second grade (Cours élémentaire 1st year) → 2nd Cycle: Basic learning
- Age 8 to 9 Third grade (Cours élémentaire 2nd year) → 2nd Cycle: Basic learning
- Age 9 to 10 Fourth grade (Cours moyen 1st year) → 3rd Cycle: Consolidation
- Age 10 to 11 Fifth grade (Cours moyen 2nd year) → 3rd Cycle: Consolidation

### Secondary School (age 11–18)

Lower secondary school or “collège” (compulsory)

- Age 11 to 12 Sixth grade (Sixième) → 4th Cycle: Further learning
- Age 12 to 13 Seventh grade (Cinquième) → 4th Cycle: Further learning
- Age 13 to 14 Eighth grade (Quatrième) → 4th Cycle: Further learning
- Age 14 to 15 Ninth grade (Troisième) → 4th Cycle: Further learning

#### Upper secondary school or “lycée”*

- Age 15 to 16 Tenth grade (Seconde) → Orientation Cycle
- Age 16 to 17 Eleventh grade (Première) → Baccalaureate route (Students choose between a general, technological, or vocational baccalaureate diploma)
- Age 17 to 18 Twelfth grade (Terminale) → Baccalaureate route

This age range does not apply to vocational upper secondary schools (lycées professionnels).

coverage: French students and workers campaign for reform (May Revolt), 1968 | Global Nonviolent Action Database
excerpt:
General strike

#### Segment Length

10 days

#### Notes on Methods

Scattered protests continued after the 3rd segment, but the methods are not clear after that point.

#### Leaders

Daniel Cohn-Bendit Jaques Sauvageot, student organization Union Nationale des Etudiants de France (UNEF) and Alain Geismar university teachers union (SNESup)

#### Partners

Confédération Générale du Travail (CGT) - communist labor union Confederation Française Démocratique de Travail (CFDT) - socialist union leftist political parties 

#### External allies

Citizens who joined the general strike, including small business owners, white collar workers, and clerical workers.

#### Involvement of social elites

Not known.

#### Nonviolent responses of opponent

Students of the radical right marched towards the Sorbonne to lead a counter-protest in response to the protest in progress by leftist students.

#### Opponents

President Charles de Gaulle and his government Radical rightist students

#### Campaigner violence

Some protests turned violent when protesters threw rocks and paving stones at police, this was in response to police initiated violence.
